components.gap: Not all of the source's actual examples are presented as given: (a) for the incoherent pair (0.3,0.4) the source reports the Kullback-Leibler closest coherent credences as C*(p)=0.438, C*(~p)=0.572 (p. 247); the chapter substitutes its own (3/7,4/7) for one explicitly chosen objective (body 573-576, annex 205-213) and never states the source's figures or that they sum to 1.01 and so are not a coherent pair; (b) the source's semi-Dutch-book example is worded as paying $1 for a $1 bet on X (p. 242), whereas body 230-235 presents a corrected version (selling X at zero, or buying the complement at one) without recording the difference; (c) the Slovic-Lichtenstein report is specifically that people do not change credences enough in response to evidence (p. 246), but body 543-545 generalizes it to unspecified reported departures in response to evidence. Present each source example as stated, then the handbook's correction or limitation.

components.gap: Most promised proofs are written (strict propriety, Brier dominance in both directions, planning, countable positive singletons, entropy and minimax uniformity, Jeffrey existence, uniqueness and noncommutativity, KL, Hellinger and variation minimal change, graded coherence with stake normalization), and the Dutch-book theorem and converse are routed to thm:p17-finite-price-coherence.
